commitResults.messageTitle: Level-0: ASCII banner and changed name to chausistant
Level-1: Echo and deals with edge cases of bye
Level-2: Add to list and view list
Level-3: mark and unmark done, and edge cases
added reading and writing to duke.txt
approved to handle edge cases and meet the two requirements
added feature that prompts user to input correct details
refactor: extract console interaction into Ui
commitResults.messageBody: Move console input, startup output, task rendering, schedule rendering, and error messages into Ui so Chausistant can focus on coordinating command and task logic. Update the UI test runner to compile every Java source file now that the application is split across classes.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: use Command enum as the command source of truth
commitResults.messageBody: Remove the duplicated command-string constants and pass Command values through task creation, task-number validation, status updates, deletion, and no-detail validation. This prevents command keywords from drifting apart and prepares the command-handling code for Parser extraction.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: introduce an executable exit command
commitResults.messageBody: Rename the existing command-keyword enum to CommandType so it remains distinct from the new Command hierarchy. Add Command and ExitCommand, then route the bye path through execute() and isExit(). This establishes the command-object seam without changing the other command paths yet.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: extract task model and TaskList
commitResults.messageBody: Move the task hierarchy and its display/save formatting into Task.java. Add TaskList as the single owner of mutable task collection operations, then adapt Chausistant to use it without changing command behavior. This prepares future Command classes to receive a focused TaskList dependency.

Add ListCommand to own rendering the current task list. Update the Command contract to receive TaskList and Ui, then route list and bye through the common command execution path. This moves another command out of Chausistant without changing user-visible behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: execute status changes through commands
commitResults.messageBody: Extract the atomic save operation into Storage and make it an explicit Command dependency. Move shared status validation, rollback, saving, and UI reporting into StatusCommand, with MarkCommand and UnmarkCommand selecting the required state. Promote ChausistantException so command classes can report the existing user-facing validation errors.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: move task loading into Storage
commitResults.messageBody: Move save-file reading, task reconstruction, malformed-line handling, and loading warnings from Chausistant into Storage. Storage now owns all file-system interactions and returns a TaskList with non-fatal warnings, leaving Chausistant to coordinate startup UI only.

Move deletion, persistence rollback, and deletion feedback into DeleteCommand. Extract numbered-task validation into NumberedTaskCommand so delete, mark, and unmark share the same task-number parsing and error messages. Chausistant now only dispatches the delete command.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: execute task creation through AddCommand
commitResults.messageBody: Extract shared task addition, save rollback, and success feedback into AddCommand. Chausistant still creates validated task objects for now, while AddCommand owns the mutation and persistence step that all task types share.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: execute schedule queries through WhatsOnCommand
commitResults.messageBody: Move event/deadline filtering, time ordering, and schedule rendering into WhatsOnCommand. Chausistant now validates the requested date and dispatches the command, while the command owns the read-only schedule behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: parse input into executable commands
commitResults.messageBody: Move command recognition, validation, task construction, and date parsing into Parser. Simplify Chausistant into an object that owns Ui, Storage, and TaskList, then follows the read-parse-execute loop. All user-visible behavior and error messages remain unchanged.

Group application, command, exception, parser, storage, task, and UI classes by responsibility. Split concrete task types into public task-package classes and update the UI test runner for packaged sources.
Verify saving nested paths, escaping task fields, and replacing old files. Cover loading missing, blank, valid, malformed, and invalid save-file paths.
Guide AI contributors to maintain tests for roughly the highest-value 50 percent of methods and update them after every code change.

created the JAR and is ready for release
